practiceDecisions.practice: Hash only published desktop assets
practiceDecisions.assessment: The unchanged hash pipelines race creation of a new output, but always enumerate a pre-existing current fragment and any older fragment. Eight finite cases distinguish both output states, both older-fragment states and both hash implementations. Candidate selection must contain only exact assets in all eight cases. Formal AI already uses an explicit asset selector. Layered run 44673787188 exposed the old negative-control ordering assumption; hosted confirmation of the corrected fixture remains pending.

practiceDecisions.assessment: Requires failed/cancelled result, no runner/steps and explicit acquisition annotation; only newest same-workflow/branch/event run, at most three attempts. Runtime and Formal AI comparison remain pending.

practiceDecisions.practice: Validate artifact paths and reject duplicate destinations before streaming ZIP payloads

practiceDecisions.assessment: Pinned lint tools, actual warnings and checked Git inventories are separate gates. Remaining transitive scripts, runtime execution and Formal AI counterparts need complete review.

practiceDecisions.practice: The execution budget remains active after its root exits
practiceDecisions.assessment: The pinned template checks its root status file before group liveness, returning success with a live finite child. The actual Formal AI production wrapper independently returns 0 in 0.07s while its child keeps stdout open for four seconds under a one-second budget. A local repair retains group liveness after root exit and passes seven finite process controls; upstream repair and exact-head hosted validation remain pending.

practiceDecisions.practice: Complete security findings and release credential preflight evidence
practiceDecisions.assessment: The six complete pinned helper/test sources are read. The template SARIF helper checks every recursively discovered nonsymlink report, findings and extraction notifications. Formal AI currently invokes CodeQL analysis without this explicit result gate. The template probes crates publish authorization without a tarball while stating that ownership still needs real publication; Formal AI records the token as unknown. Both registry preflights open a session but ignore cancellation failures. Cargo own-manifest warnings need a separate check from rustc deny-warnings. Applicable adoption, runtime regressions and hosted proof remain unfinished.

practiceDecisions.practice: Parsed version identity and branch authorization
practiceDecisions.assessment: Template check-version-modification parses package/workspace version identity and never grants a release exemption from an untrusted branch name. The fully read Formal AI counterpart still uses a whole-document version regex and grants four release-prefix exemptions. Its head-versus-current-base comparison deliberately handles merged base versions and moved manifests and must be preserved when repairing identity and authorization. Applicable repairs and native behavioral verification remain unfinished.

practiceDecisions.practice: Release registry uncertainty and fallible outputs
practiceDecisions.assessment: Configured output writes in six callers now use the shared fatal writer (284e24430); all seven native output cases pass in exact-head core job 136080808912 at 11c0bd05. The ordinary registry path still conflates some unavailable observations with missing artifacts, and its repair remains unfinished. Preserve immutable all-target recovery checks.

practiceDecisions.practice: Committed binary lockfile enforcement
practiceDecisions.assessment: Template check-cargo-lock resolves selected package identity from Cargo metadata and requires a binary lockfile to exist in the HEAD commit. Formal AI has no same-named helper, while its dependency audit enumerates tracked locks and Rust CI uses locked inputs. A full equivalent-behavior decision remains unfinished.

practiceDecisions.practice: Registry uncertainty, crate publication and package path helpers
practiceDecisions.assessment: Fully read the four complete pinned helpers. Registry metadata parsing, bounded HTTP requests and distinctions between absence and transient/permanent failures are applicable comparison inputs. Rate-limit publication deferral, Cargo credential-store fallback and dependent-job ownership need actual Formal AI workflow/counterpart comparison and executable evidence. No implementation or upstream-repair credit is established by this read.

practiceDecisions.practice: Release-source and Git-index ownership
practiceDecisions.assessment: The template validates committed tree identities, restricts release-only mutations using parsed TOML/JSON equivalence, rejects unrelated staged/untracked/modified paths, distinguishes ruleset refusals from lost races, and verifies changelog/lock writes before publication. Formal AI already has staged release authority; preserve its tested-artifact identity rather than transplanting the standalone release writer. The whole-text package-version regex and optional missing-lock cases still require counterpart experiments.

practiceDecisions.assessment: The template seconds-only fs::write creator remains an upstream reproduction/report task. Template collection and new-fragment policy comparison remain unfinished.

practiceDecisions.practice: Crate release identity, package size and downstream smoke tests
practiceDecisions.assessment: The template bounds registry-version collision attempts, fails Actions output writes, distinguishes duplicate-tag release API failures, caps release text, installs an exact published version and compiles a fresh dependent crate. The size checker hard-codes target/package, the entrypoint parser only recognizes literal table syntax and existing CLI capture is unbounded; none supersedes Formal AI bounded qualified-artifact observation. Formal counterparts and workflow callers must establish applicability and verification.

practiceDecisions.practice: Whole-request change classification and job-local tool installation
practiceDecisions.assessment: Change detection covers the full synthetic merge against its base, preserves successful empty diffs, checks original parents to reject unavailable shallow history, and includes deleted paths without rename hiding. Its newline path decoding and broad language exclusions need comparison with Formal AI Git-safe admission closure. Tool installation is checked per job and before first use, but the parser is indentation/substring based and does not prove conditional installation executes.

practiceDecisions.practice: Size-check traversal and annotation ownership
practiceDecisions.assessment: Separate source/documentation thresholds, whole-component directory pruning and escaped annotations are applicable practices; Formal AI has a language/data-aware size policy that must be preserved. Template traversal silently drops directory/read errors, and changed-file whitespace splitting is not Git-path safe. Do not import these weaker failure semantics.

practiceDecisions.practice: Link-check recovery and archive evidence
practiceDecisions.assessment: Both consumers validate complete timeout/error counts and reject checker runtime/configuration failures. Retries are limited to transient/transport failures; permanent verdicts remain failed, bodies are cancelled, and recovery gates cover the whole report. Archive lookup uncertainty remains distinct from confirmed absence. Formal AI counterparts need exact comparison with current maintained tests; historical filename caches or mocked lookup success do not establish live link health.

Compare the maintained Formal AI scanner installation/lock and CI version constraints without copying template package identity or treating transitive package lists as independent practices.
